chains.title: C250T creates a de novo ETS site occupied by GABPA (GABP complex), activating TERT

links.claim: The alt allele creates a GGAA ETS core: Ets group G003 passes strongly with alt binding more (best model ETV5 z 167.5; site strength ref 94.8th to alt 99.9th percentile), and GABPA has its own passing QBiC-SELEX model (z 71.32) and is expressed at 15.5 TPM in glioblastoma lines. Within this group I chose GABPA over ETV5/ELF1 on two pieces of cited evidence rather than on the SELEX ranking: ENCODE ChIP-seq shows GABPA peaks containing this exact position in two biosamples (E16), while no ELF1 peak contains or lies within 100 bp of it (E17), and the published mechanism at mutant TERT promoters is selective GABPA recruitment (E18b). The GABP heterotetramer/second-ETS-site spacing model is background knowledge, not shown by the cited evidence.

The variant lies inside promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 with high DNase, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac (z-scores are maxima across biosamples, so GBM-specific activity is not shown), and VEP annotates a promoter regulatory feature; GABPA ChIP peaks in HepG2 and SK-N-SH show this element is TF-occupied in at least some cell types.

The element is the TERT core promoter (TERT TSS 0 kb); CLPTM1L is 50 kb away. Assignment is by promoter identity and proximity only - no eQTL, CRISPR or allele-specific expression evidence is cited, and the cCRE also lists MIR4457 and CLPTM1L.

GABPA is expressed in glioblastoma lines (15.5 TPM) and TERT promoter mutations are among the most frequent alterations in IDH-wildtype GBM; occupancy of this site has been shown in HepG2 and SK-N-SH, not in GBM tumour cells, so lineage specificity is inferred, not demonstrated.

If TERT is transcriptionally reactivated, telomerase activity is restored, which is the common molecular feature of TERTp-mutant melanoma and GBM and whose loss triggers senescence; the cited quotes are generic to TERTp mutations and do not test GABPA specifically.

TERT is the promoter's own gene at 0 kb; assignment is proximity-based only.
ELF1 and related class I ETS factors listed in G003 are expressed at tens of TPM in glioblastoma lines; no occupancy evidence in this lineage is cited.
Higher TERT transcription restores telomerase and supports tumour growth; the cited quotes do not implicate ELF1.

chains.title: Loss of MBD1 binding de-represses the TERT promoter

links.claim: MBD1 has its own QBiC-SELEX model that loses binding on the alt allele (z -41.31, effect -1.236; ref 100th to alt 98.6th percentile) and is expressed at 31.5 TPM; the SELEX assay uses unmethylated DNA, so this does not demonstrate methyl-CpG-dependent binding at this site.
The site lies in the TERT promoter-like cCRE; no methylation or CpG-density evidence is cited for this element.
If MBD1 represses at the TERT core promoter, its loss would raise TERT; no cited evidence shows MBD1 regulates TERT.
MBD1 is expressed in glioblastoma lines (31.5 TPM); occupancy at TERT is not shown.
De-repressed TERT would restore telomerase and avert senescence; the cited quotes are generic.

chains.title: ELF3/ETV6-type ETS specificity (group G020) mediates the gain, with ETV6 the only expressed member

links.claim: Group G020 has the largest per-model effect (5.168 for ELF3, alt binds more); ELF3/ELF5/ETV7 are below 0.5 TPM, so within the group I chose ETV6 (own model, z 46.24, 5.65 TPM) as the only expressed member - the large effect size belongs to ELF3, not ETV6, so the quantitative support for ETV6 is weaker.
The gained site is inside the active promoter-like cCRE at TERT.
TERT is the gene of this promoter; proximity only.
ETV6 expression in glioblastoma lines is low (5.65 TPM) and no occupancy at this site is shown.
ETV6 is generally a repressor, so gained ETV6 binding would be expected to lower rather than raise TERT; this chain therefore does not readily explain telomerase reactivation in TERTp-mutant tumours.

grades_v0.reason: GABPA has its own model that passes (z 71.32, alt binds more) and is expressed at 15.5 TPM, but this is only an in-vitro binding prediction. The pick of GABPA over ETV5/ELF1 rests on prior knowledge of the GABP mechanism, not on cited evidence. No ChIP or perturbation data is cited, and the second native ETS site and its spacing are not shown in any evidence.

E03 places the variant inside PLS cCRE EH38E3622530 with high DNase, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac, and E01 annotates a promoter regulatory feature. The z-scores are maxima over biosamples, so GBM specificity is not shown, but the element link itself is well covered.

E02 and E01 show TERT at 0 kb and a TERT upstream consequence, which is proximity only. No eQTL, perturbation or allele-specific expression data is cited. The ENCODE cCRE also lists MIR4457 and CLPTM1L as nearby genes.

E04f shows TERTp mutations are frequent in IDH-wt GBM, and E06 gives a GABPA TPM from DepMap. Neither shows that GABPA occupies this site in GBM tumour cells, and the epigenomic maxima are not biosample-specific.

E04a supports TERT promoter mutations and telomerase activation in melanoma, and E04e shows TERT loss triggers senescence. Neither links this variant's GABPA mechanism to the phenotype in GBM or bladder. The claim of unlimited proliferation and progression over-reaches the cited quotes.

ELF1 passes (z 164.23, alt binds more) and is expressed at 17.4 TPM, but ELF1 was chosen from the Ets group without cited evidence. The claim of a canonical GGAA site without GABP spacing is not shown. This is a binding prediction alone.
E03 and E01 show the variant sits in an active promoter-like cCRE at TERT.
Nearest-gene proximity (E02) only. No functional link from the variant to TERT expression is cited.
E06 gives ELF1 expression only as a TPM, with no evidence of occupancy in GBM. 'Class I ETS' as a group is claimed, but only the listed TFs have TPMs shown.
E04a and E04f give generic TERTp mutation prevalence and do not tie ELF1 to telomerase restoration.

MBD1 passes with alt binding less (z -41.31) and is expressed. However, MBD1 binds methylated CpG, and a prediction from in-vitro SELEX with unmethylated DNA does not show a repressive role here. A binding prediction alone is at best weak.
E03 supports a promoter cCRE but contains no CpG or methylation data. 'CpG-rich' is asserted without evidence.
Nothing cited shows MBD1 represses TERT. E01 and E02 only show proximity. The repressor role is assumed.
E09 gives MBD1 expression of 31.5 TPM only. This shows presence, not occupancy at TERT.
E04a and E04e show telomerase effects in general terms and do not support MBD1 loss as the cause. The direction is consistent with de-repression, but no evidence supports it.

G020 shows alt gain, but the best models (ELF3/ELF5) are essentially unexpressed. ETV6 was picked only as the expressed member, and it is a weaker model (z 46.24) that is typically a repressor. The effect 5.168 belongs to ELF3, not ETV6.
E03 shows the variant is in a promoter-like cCRE.
Proximity only (E02), with no functional evidence.
ETV6 at 5.65 TPM is low, and the chain itself admits the effect could be opposite. No occupancy evidence is cited.
The chain concedes that a repressive ETV6 would fail to explain the phenotype. E04a does not bear on ETV6.

grades_final.reason: G003 alt-gain and GABPA's own passing model (z 71.32) are only a binding prediction. The ChIP peaks in HepG2 and SK-N-SH (E16) are not allele-specific and are not from GBM. E18b describes GABPA recruitment to mutant TERT promoters but is not allele-specific evidence for this variant. E18a says canonical mutations create ETS sites, but names no TF. The GABPA choice over ELF1 rests on indirect context. The ELF1 ChIP absence (E17) may only reflect missing experiments. No perturbation evidence is cited.

The variant lies in PLS cCRE EH38E3622530 with high DNase, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac, and VEP gives a promoter feature. These z-scores are maxima over biosamples and are not GBM-specific. This is epigenomic context only, with no perturbation or genetic evidence for element function.

TERT is at 0 kb from the TSS and the cCRE is its promoter, but assignment is by proximity only. No eQTL, CRISPR or allele-specific expression evidence is cited, and the cCRE also lists MIR4457 and CLPTM1L.

GABPA expression of 15.5 TPM in DepMap GBM lines and TERTp mutations being frequent in IDH-wildtype GBM (E04f) are consistent with the claim. GABPA occupancy is shown only in HepG2 and SK-N-SH, so the GBM link is inferred.

E04a, E04e and E04f show that TERTp mutations are common in melanoma and GBM and that TERT loss triggers senescence. They are generic to TERTp mutations and do not test C250T, GABPA or TERT reactivation by this variant. They are consistent with the phenotype but indirect.

ELF1 has a passing own model (z 164.23) with alt binding more, which is only a binding prediction. The chain admits the screen cannot separate ELF1 from GABPA. No ELF1 ChIP peak is found, though that may reflect missing experiments. No evidence selects ELF1 over other class I ETS factors.
The PLS cCRE overlapping the variant is active by epigenomic markers, but the z-scores are maxima over biosamples and give no allele or ELF1-specific support.
Proximity to TERT (0 kb) is the only support. No eQTL, CRISPR or allele-specific expression evidence is cited.
ELF1 and related class I ETS factors are expressed at tens of TPM in GBM lines (E06). This is expression context only and the chain cites no occupancy evidence in this lineage.
The quotes support telomerase activation in TERTp-mutant tumours generically. The chain itself notes they do not implicate ELF1, so the cited evidence is only indirect.

MBD1 has an own-model prediction of reduced alt binding (z -41.31). This is only a binding prediction, and the chain notes that SELEX uses unmethylated DNA, so methyl-CpG-dependent MBD1 binding is not shown. MBD1 occupancy is not shown in any ChIP peak or perturbation. Weak at best.
The cCRE is promoter-like and active, but no methylation or CpG evidence is cited for it, so the MBD1 repressive role is unsupported. This is generic element context.
E01 and E02 only show TERT is the nearest gene. No cited evidence shows MBD1 regulates TERT, as the chain itself acknowledges.
MBD1 is expressed at 31.5 TPM in GBM lines. This is expression context only and occupancy at TERT is not shown.
The quotes are generic to TERT reactivation. They do not bear on MBD1 or on a de-repression mechanism.

G020 shows alt-gain predictions, but the large effect belongs to ELF3, which is not expressed. ETV6 is chosen only by expression, and its own model (z 46.24) is a binding prediction alone with no ChIP or perturbation evidence.
The variant lies in an active PLS cCRE (E03). The z-scores are maxima over biosamples, so this is generic context with no ETV6-specific support.
Proximity to TERT only (E02). No eQTL, CRISPR or allele-specific expression evidence is cited.
ETV6 expression is low (5.65 TPM) and no occupancy is shown. Only expression context is cited, so the support is thin.

The chain argues ETV6 is a repressor, so gained binding would lower TERT, contradicting the TERT activation seen in TERTp-mutant tumours. E04a does not support an ETV6-mediated phenotype, and the direction is inconsistent.

A major molecular feature of melanoma is abnormal telomerase activation; this is most often caused by telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations, which occur in 50-82% of cases and are the most common noncoding alteration in this cancer.
CDKN2A and CDK4 mutations act through UV-dependent and cell cycle disruption pathways, while BAP1, POT1, and TERT mutations are considered UV-independent.
The single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs2853669, also located in the TERT promoter, may influence telomerase activity, though its clinical relevance in GBM remains unclear.

Patients carrying the SNP and TPM on the same allele (C/C and T/C cis) had shorter overall survival than those carrying them on different alleles (T/T or T/C trans; 19 vs 25 months, p = 0.048), and TERT expression was also lower in this group (p = 0.038).
Additionally, loss of either USP10 or FOXM1 suppresses the expression of the downstream target Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), triggering cellular senescence.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations are among the most frequent molecular alterations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type glioblastoma (GBM), yet the molecular profiles and prognostic implications associated with TERTp status remain incompletely characterized.

PMID 33483600 (2021): Synergistic activation of mutant TERT promoter by Sp1 and GABPA in BRAF<sup>V600E</sup>-driven human cancers.

Canonical TERTp mutations create de novo binding sites for ETS family transcription factors that induce favourable conditions for DNA damage formation by UV light, thus creating a hotspot effect but only after a first mutational hit.

Here, we report that transcription factor GABPA mediates the regulation of BRAFV600E/MAPK signaling on TERT reactivation by selectively recruiting activated ERK to mutant TERT promoter, where activated ERK can phosphorylate Sp1, thereby resulting in HDAC1 dissociation and an active chromatin state.
